messages.subject: what to make of datadist warning message in lrm
messages.subject_clean: what to make of datadist warning message in lrm
messages.body_plain:
I'm studying diachronic change in Old French, specifically change in subject-verb order over the course of about three centuries. The dataframe consists of embedded V2 clauses with overt non-pronominal subjects contiguous to the verb (which thus excludes any clauses in which the subject has been wh-extracted). I have successfully fitted a binary logistic model (although it’s not a wonderful fit) using glm with date and clause-type as independent variables. When I run rlm to get further helpful statistics, I get a warning message:

Warning message:

In Design(eval.parent(m)) :

  Variable cltype has levels cnjctl advbl nonSwh which do not match levels given to datadist ( cnjctl advbl nonSwh Swh ). datadist values ignored.

I’m not sure how much to trust the resulting statistics if the datadist is ignored. I’m attaching a stucture-summary of the dataframe, the output of glm, and the output of lrm. I’d appreciate any pointers anyone has to offer. Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] what to make of datadist warning message in lrm
messages.subject_clean: [StatForLing with R] what to make of datadist warning message in lrm
messages.body_plain:
The warning says it all, I think: your variable cltype has levels that
are not attested: the frequency of cltype: SwH is 0 in your summary.
I'd say you should run this line before you define the model:

V2EMBCLSDATESVVS <- droplevels(V2EMBCLSDATESVVS)

then define the datadist object, and only then run the model.

messages.body_plain: I'm studying diachronic change in Old French, specifically change in subject-verb order over the course of about three centuries. The dataframe consists of embedded V2 clauses with overt pronominal subjects contiguous to the verb (which thus excludes any clauses in which the subject has been wh-extracted). I have successfully fitted a binary logistic model (although it’s not a wonderful fit) using glm with date and clause-type as independent variables. However, lrm, from which I'd like to get a loglikelihood ratio (G), Nagelkerke's R-squared, and C values, can't fit a model. I feel certain that these could be calculated by hand in R, but my math background is insufficient to get me there. messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] getting additional stats when lrm won't run
messages.subject_clean: [StatForLing with R] getting additional stats when lrm won't run
messages.body_plain:
Try this:

##########################################
logregR2s <- function (final.model) {
   require(Hmisc, quietly = TRUE)
   if (class(final.model)[1] == "lrm") {
      final.model <- glm(formula(final.model), family = binomial)
      cv <- final.model[[3]]
   }
   if (class(final.model$data) == "environment") {
      null.model <- glm(as.formula(paste(as.character(formula(final.model))[2],
                                         "~ 1")), family = binomial)
   }
   else {
      null.model <- glm(as.formula(paste(as.character(formula(final.model))[2],
                                         "~ 1")), family = binomial,
data = final.model$data)
   }
   mf <- 1 - (as.numeric(logLik(final.model))/as.numeric(logLik(null.model)))
   sample.size <- length(predict(final.model))
   cs <- 1 - exp((-2 * (as.numeric(logLik(final.model)) -
as.numeric(logLik(null.model))))/sample.size)
   nk <- cs/(1 - exp(2 * as.numeric(logLik(null.model))/sample.size))
   llr <- final.model$null.deviance - final.model$deviance
   df <- final.model$df.null - final.model$df.residual
   pv <- pchisq(llr, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
   if (class(final.model$data) == "environment") {
      cv <- as.numeric(somers2(predict(final.model),
as.numeric(get(as.character(formula(final.model)[2]))) -
                                  1))[1]
   }
   else {
      cv <- as.numeric(somers2(predict(final.model), with(final.model$data,

as.numeric(get(as.character(formula(final.model)[2])))) -
                                  1))[1]
   }
   output <- list(Correlations = c(`McFadden's R2` = mf, `Cox &
Snell's R2` = cs,
                                   `Nagelkerke's R2` = nk, C = cv),
Significance = c(`LL ratio` = llr,

              Df = df, `p-value` = pv))
   return(output)
}

logregR2s(Spinv.glm)
##########################################

Best,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
----------------------------------
Univ. of California, Santa Barbara
http://tinyurl.com/stgries
